newsitem.title: GERMANY: Tietmeyer - France sees stable franc-mark as important.
newsitem.headline: Tietmeyer - France sees stable franc-mark as important.

text.p: Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer said on Sunday that French monetary policy was running on a stable course and that he saw no risk to the franc-deutschemark exchange rate from the new government.
In an interview with German radio, Tietmeyer said the French were aware of the importance of stable exchange rates with other European countries.
"I believe that French monetary policy is on a very stable course and I assume that the franc-mark relationship is not up for discussion," Tietmeyer said.

Noting that the franc-mark relation had been relatively stable of late, Tietmeyer said: "If I have understood the politics correctly, the new government will do what it can not to put this result at risk."
Tietmeyer also denied that the Bundesbank had declared patronage for the French franc in the past, but he said it had helped the franc to win market trust in the past.
"And I see no reason why this should not be also so in the future. Declarations of patronage are not necessary," he said.

Tietmeyer noted that the job creation schemes being mooted in France ran counter to previous policies but said policies were still at an early stage and had not translated into concrete budget strategies.
"We must wait and see. But I am convinced that people in France see very clearly how important a stable exchange rate between the French franc and the other European currencies is."
